headline: You build data pipelines in deliberate steps, asking tests to prove both that the data is right and that the guardrails work.

archetype.name: The Guardrail Engineer
archetype.description: You approach data engineering through concrete failure cases: lost leading zeros, duplicate transactions, exposed customer details, and checks that should reject bad models. Your prompts often move from a focused design question to a small implementation, with tests and documentation close behind. You give your assistant short directions, but the acceptance criteria have teeth.

dimensions.title: Prove the failure first
dimensions.summary: You frequently ask for tests before implementation and want to see safeguards fail on purpose before trusting them. You also stage changes through design, inspection, and small implementation decisions, keeping the work reviewable.

evidence.quote: test 先跑一次確認會 fail，我想看到 red 再改 code
先設計不要寫 code
這個 macro 的 test 怎麼寫？我想要先看到它擋下一個故意放錯的 model

dimensions.title: Short requests, precise boundaries
dimensions.summary: You write concise Traditional Chinese requests with English technical terms, often adding requirements through brief follow-ups. Your instructions specify observable behavior, naming preferences, and practical constraints, with occasional thanks and informal English.

evidence.quote: 麻煩先幫我寫 test，再寫 function：把 CSV 的 amount 欄位轉成 Decimal，空字串要變 None

好，CI 改成 uv sync --frozen，謝謝

dimensions.title: From ingestion to BI
dimensions.summary: Your requests span Python ingestion, dbt warehouse transformations, and Dagster orchestration, including snapshots, sensors, and asset checks. You also specify packaging and CI conventions, with requests for uv, strict typing, linting, and automated tests.

evidence.quote: quick question：pandas read_csv 的 dtype=str 跟 converters 哪個比較適合處理混亂的欄位？

CI 用 GitHub Actions 跑 ruff、mypy 跟 pytest，matrix 跑 3.12 和 3.13

dimensions.title: Correctness with privacy built in
dimensions.summary: You repeatedly focus on preserving data meaning: exact amounts, intact identifiers, and protection against duplicate writes. Privacy appears as an implementation requirement across logs, notifications, and warehouse models. You also ask documentation to explain units, setup, and the reasons behind technical decisions.

dimensions.title: Compare, choose, apply
dimensions.summary: You use focused comparisons to understand a concept, then turn the answer into a concrete implementation choice. Your follow-ups connect those choices to source limitations, consistent conventions, and meaningful tests.
